# Story 1.1: Enrol an authenticator app
Status: ready-for-dev

## Story
As an account holder, I want to enrol an authenticator app by scanning a QR code, so that I can protect my sign-in with a time-based one-time password.

## Acceptance Criteria
- AC-1: Given a signed-in account holder with no confirmed authenticator, when they open the enrolment page, then a QR code is shown that their authenticator app can scan.
- AC-2: Given the QR code is shown, when they submit a code generated by their app, then enrolment is marked complete and 2FA is enabled for the account.
- AC-3: Given the QR code is shown, when they submit a code that does not match the secret, then enrolment is not completed and they see an error.

## Tasks / Subtasks
- [ ] Add pyotp and the `totp_secret` column on the users table (AC: 1)
- [ ] Generate a TOTP secret for the account and render the QR code on the enrolment page (AC: 1)
- [ ] Verify the submitted code with pyotp and mark enrolment complete only on a match (AC: 2)
- [ ] Reject a non-matching code with an error and leave enrolment incomplete (AC: 3)
- [ ] Test the QR page, the accepted code, and the rejected code (AC: 1, 2, 3)

## Dev Notes
- FR-1 is the requirement behind this story.
- Architecture: `totp_secret` is a new column on the users table, and verification uses pyotp inside the existing Flask app. No new service.
- Enrolment stays incomplete until a code is confirmed, so the stored secret alone does not turn on 2FA. Sign-in gating is in Story 1.2.

- [Source: docs/architecture.md#data-model]

# Story 1.2: Require a TOTP code at sign-in
Status: ready-for-dev

## Story
As an account holder with 2FA enabled, I want sign-in to require a valid TOTP code after my password, so that a stolen password alone cannot sign me in.

## Acceptance Criteria
- AC-1: Given an account with 2FA enabled, when the correct password is submitted, then the user is asked for a TOTP code and no session is created yet.
- AC-2: Given the TOTP prompt, when a valid current code is submitted, then sign-in completes and the user receives a session.
- AC-3: Given the TOTP prompt, when an invalid code is submitted, then sign-in is refused and no session is created.
- AC-4: Given an account without 2FA enabled, when the correct password is submitted, then the user is signed in without a code prompt.

## Tasks / Subtasks
- [ ] Insert a TOTP step after the password check, applied only to accounts with 2FA enabled (AC: 1, 4)
- [ ] Verify the submitted code against `totp_secret` with pyotp (AC: 2, 3)
- [ ] Create the session only after a valid TOTP code (AC: 2)
- [ ] Refuse an invalid code and create no session (AC: 3)
- [ ] Test the four sign-in cases (AC: 1, 2, 3, 4)

## Dev Notes
- FR-2 is the requirement behind this story.
- Architecture: TOTP verification uses pyotp in the existing Flask login route. No new service.
- The session cookie is issued only after the second step succeeds.

### References
- [Source: docs/prd.md#FR-2]
- [Source: docs/architecture.md#verification]

# Story 1.3: Recover sign-in with a recovery code
Status: ready-for-dev

## Story
As an account holder, I want ten single-use recovery codes issued when I enrol, so that I can still sign in if I lose my device.

## Acceptance Criteria
- AC-1: Given an account holder who has just confirmed enrolment, when enrolment completes, then they are shown exactly ten recovery codes.
- AC-2: Given the TOTP prompt, when one of the account's unused recovery codes is submitted in place of a TOTP code, then sign-in completes and that code is consumed.
- AC-3: Given the TOTP prompt, when a used recovery code or a value that is not one of the account's codes is submitted, then sign-in is refused.

## Tasks / Subtasks
- [ ] Generate ten recovery codes at enrolment completion and store them in the `recovery_codes` column (AC: 1)
- [ ] Show the ten codes to the user when enrolment completes (AC: 1)
- [ ] Accept an unused recovery code at the TOTP prompt and mark it consumed (AC: 2)
- [ ] Refuse a used or unknown recovery code (AC: 3)
- [ ] Test issuance, single use, and refusal (AC: 1, 2, 3)

## Dev Notes
- FR-3 is the requirement behind this story.
- Architecture: the `recovery_codes` column is added to the users table. No new service.
- Each code replaces a TOTP code for one sign-in only. The TOTP prompt from Story 1.2 is where codes are accepted.

### References
- [Source: docs/prd.md#FR-3]
- [Source: docs/architecture.md#data-model]

Not added as stories (no requirement asks for them):
- Storage of recovery codes: the input doesn't say whether they are hashed. Decide before the dev pair builds Story 1.3.
- Disabling 2FA, regenerating recovery codes, and replay protection for a TOTP code already used in the same window are not covered by any requirement.

# Story 1.1: Enrol an authenticator app
Status: ready-for-dev

## Story
As an account holder, I want to enrol an authenticator app by scanning a QR code, so that I can protect my sign-in with one-time codes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- AC-1: Given a signed-in user with no authenticator enrolled, when they open the 2FA enrolment page, then they see a QR code for a new TOTP secret and the same secret as text for manual entry.
- AC-2: Given the enrolment page is showing, when the user submits the six-digit code their app generates from that secret, then enrolment completes and the account shows 2FA as enabled.
- AC-3: Given the enrolment page is showing, when the user submits an incorrect code, then enrolment does not complete, the account still shows 2FA as disabled, and the user sees an error and can retry with the same QR code.
- AC-4: Given a user who opened the enrolment page but has not confirmed a code, when they sign in, then they are not asked for a second factor.

## Tasks / Subtasks
- [ ] Add the `totp_secret` column to the users table (AC: 2, 4)
- [ ] Generate a TOTP secret with pyotp and hold it in the session until confirmation (AC: 1, 4)
- [ ] Render the enrolment page with the QR code and the manual secret (AC: 1)
- [ ] Verify the submitted code with pyotp and write `totp_secret` only when it passes (AC: 2)
- [ ] Show an error on a wrong code and keep the enrolment pending (AC: 3)

## Dev Notes
- FR-1 is the requirement behind this story.
- Architecture: `totp_secret` is a column on the users table, and pyotp does generation and verification with no new service. Because there is no status column, the unconfirmed secret must stay out of `totp_secret` until a code verifies. That keeps an unconfirmed enrolment from enabling 2FA.

As an API client, I want a request over my key's limit to be rejected with a Retry-After header, so that I know when to try again.

## Acceptance Criteria
- AC-1: Given an API key whose counter has reached the default limit in the current window, when it sends another request, then the response is 429 and the endpoint handler is not invoked.
- AC-2: Given a 429 response, when the client reads it, then the Retry-After header is a whole number of seconds until the current window resets.
- AC-3: Given an API key whose counter is under the default limit, when it sends a request, then the request is served normally and is not rejected.

## Tasks / Subtasks
- [ ] Increment the per-key request counter in Redis on each request, with the counter expiring at the end of its window (AC: 1, 3)
- [ ] Reject a request whose key's counter exceeds the default limit with 429, before the handler runs (AC: 1)
- [ ] Add Retry-After to the 429 response, set to the seconds remaining in the window (AC: 2)
- [ ] Test: exceed the default limit and assert 429 plus a positive integer Retry-After (AC: 1, 2)
- [ ] Test: a key under the limit is served normally (AC: 3)

## Dev Notes
- FR-1 is the requirement behind this story.
- Architecture: Redis is the counter store, so the counter lives in Redis, not in process memory.
- Builds the limiter that stories 1.2 and 1.3 extend.

# Story 1.2: Give an API key a custom limit
Status: ready-for-dev

## Story
As an API operator, I want to give one API key a custom limit that overrides the default, so that integration partners who burst above the default keep working unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria
- AC-1: Given an API key with a custom limit above the default, when it sends requests above the default but within its custom limit, then each request is served and none is rejected with 429.
- AC-2: Given an API key with a custom limit, when it sends more requests than that limit in the current window, then the response is 429 with a Retry-After header.
- AC-3: Given an API key with no custom limit, when it sends requests over the default limit, then it is rejected with 429 as in story 1.1.

## Tasks / Subtasks
- [ ] Add a nullable limit column to the api_keys table, where null means the default applies (AC: 1, 2, 3)
- [ ] Have the limiter read the key's limit from api_keys and use it in place of the default when set (AC: 1, 2, 3)
- [ ] Test: a key with a custom limit above the default is served for requests above the default and within the custom limit (AC: 1)
- [ ] Test: a key with a custom limit is rejected with 429 and Retry-After past that limit (AC: 2)
- [ ] Test: a key with a null limit is rejected at the default limit (AC: 3)

## Dev Notes
- FR-2 is the requirement behind this story.
- Architecture: limits are per API key, read from the existing api_keys table, which has no limit column yet, so this story adds it.
- Depends on the limiter from story 1.1.

# Story 1.3: Counters survive an application restart
Status: ready-for-dev

## Story
As an API client, I want my remaining request budget to survive a service restart, so that a restart does not give me a fresh budget.

## Acceptance Criteria
- AC-1: Given a client has used part of its budget, when the application restarts, then the next request counts against the remaining budget, not a fresh one.
- AC-2: Given a client has exhausted its budget in the current window, when the application restarts before the window ends, then its next request is rejected with 429 and a Retry-After header.

## Tasks / Subtasks
- [ ] Keep limiter state only in Redis, with no in-process counter cache or fallback (AC: 1, 2)
- [ ] Name counter keys by API key and window so a new process resolves the same keys (AC: 1, 2)
- [ ] Test: consume part of the budget, restart the application process, and assert the next request sees the remaining count (AC: 1)
- [ ] Test: exhaust the budget, restart the application process, and assert 429 with Retry-After (AC: 2)

## Dev Notes
- CAP-1 is the requirement behind this story.
- Architecture: Redis is the counter store, so counter state is held outside the application process and survives its restart.
